b2-28-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning a Talk
b2-28-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how you will organise your short talk at the office. You will speak about three points: the price, the date and the place.
b2-28-01.prompt: Tell Meg the order of the three points of your talk.
cues: Say what you will talk about first
b2-28-01.target: En primer lugar, hablaré del precio; en segundo lugar, de la fecha; por último, del lugar.
b2-28-01.english: First, I will talk about the price; second, about the date; lastly, about the place.
b2-28-01.canDo: I can order the points of a talk with en primer lugar, en segundo lugar and por último.

b2-28-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Side Remark
b2-28-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos about the plan for the weekend and you suddenly remember something: you need to know if he has the tickets.
b2-28-02.prompt: Tell Carlos your plan and add a side remark with a question.
cues: Say what you plan to do
Add a side remark with a question about the tickets
b2-28-02.target: Mañana vamos al cine; por cierto, ¿ya compraste los boletos?
b2-28-02.english: Tomorrow we are going to the cinema; by the way, have you already bought the tickets?
b2-28-02.canDo: I can add a side remark with por cierto, a propósito (de) and dicho sea de paso.

b2-28-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Moving On
b2-28-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about Saturday's dinner. You have just settled the date, and now you divide the food and the drinks between you.
b2-28-03.prompt: Tell Meg that the date is settled, then say who takes the food and who takes the drinks.
cues: Move on from the date to the next point
b2-28-03.target: Pues bien, ya tenemos la fecha. En cuanto a la comida, yo cocino; en cuanto a las bebidas, las traes tú.
b2-28-03.english: Well then, we have the date. As for the food, I will cook; as for the drinks, you bring them.
b2-28-03.canDo: I can move on to the next step with pues bien.

b2-28-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of Living Downtown
b2-28-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about living in the centre of Budapest. You see two sides: it is comfortable, and it is expensive.
b2-28-04.prompt: Give Carlos the two sides of living in the centre.
b2-28-04.target: Por una parte, vivir en el centro es cómodo; por otra, es caro.
b2-28-04.english: On the one hand, living in the centre is comfortable; on the other, it is expensive.
b2-28-04.canDo: I can set two sides of a point against each other with por una parte … por otra.

b2-28-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Closing an Opinion
b2-28-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think of the plan to have dinner at home on Saturday. The plan is cheap and easy.
b2-28-05.prompt: Give Meg your opinion of the plan and close with a final judgement.
cues: Say why the plan is good
Close your opinion with a closing marker
b2-28-05.target: El plan es barato y fácil. En definitiva, me parece una buena idea.
b2-28-05.english: The plan is cheap and easy. All in all, I think it is a good idea.
b2-28-05.canDo: I can close a text with en resumen, en conclusión, en definitiva or en suma.

b2-28-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Telling the Plan in Order
b2-28-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to tell him the plan for Saturday in order and then to sum it up.
b2-28-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos the plan in order and close with a summary.
cues: Give the three steps in order
b2-28-consolidation.target: En primer lugar, compramos la comida; en segundo lugar, cocinamos; por último, cenamos. En resumen, será una noche tranquila.
b2-28-consolidation.english: First, we buy the food; second, we cook; lastly, we have dinner. To sum up, it will be a quiet evening.
b2-28-consolidation.canDo: I can structure a short talk from a first point to a closing summary.
